title: New Zealand’s final election count leaves the governing coalition one seat short
seoTitle: New Zealand election results: why the coalition fell one seat short
dek: The final count gives the governing parties 65 of Parliament’s 130 seats. The Opportunity Party’s seven seats give it a say in whether the coalition can return to power.
happened: New Zealand’s Electoral Commission released the official count on November 27, including ballots cast overseas and other special votes. National fell from 42 seats on election night to 40. National, ACT and New Zealand First together hold 65 seats, one short of a majority. Labour, the Greens and Te Pāti Māori hold 58 between them.

sides.says: Caretaker Prime Minister Christopher Luxon said he was confident he could reach an agreement with Opportunity and his existing coalition partners. He said negotiations could take time.

Party leader Qiulae Wong said she would consider joining a coalition or agreeing to back a government on confidence and budget votes. She said her party would hold to its policy priorities, including stronger climate action.
Leader Chris Hipkins acknowledged that the parties on the left would still fall one seat short of a majority even with Opportunity’s support.

next: The parties must work out whether they can support a government. The Electoral Commission expects to return the formal election writ on December 3 if nobody applies for a recount.
summary: New Zealand’s final election count cost the governing coalition its majority. Christopher Luxon now needs support from outside the existing coalition to lead a majority government.
